title: もはや
simpleExplanation: もはや is an adverb meaning "by now (things have changed so much that)": もはや手遅れだ (it is already too late), もはや若くない (no longer young). It stresses that a situation has reached a point of no return. With a negative it means "no longer"; with an affirmative it means "already, by now".
whenUsed: Formal written Japanese and serious speech: commentary, essays, dramatic dialogue. Stronger and more final than もう. Typical predicates: 手遅れだ・不可能だ・〜ない・珍しくない・当たり前だ.
formation: Set: もはや手遅れだ / もはやこれまでだ (this is the end)

diagram.title: From もう to もはや

items.label: 今や
items.description: now (a new situation has arrived, often positive)

items.label: もはや
items.description: by now, irreversibly (formal, final, often resigned)

examples.note: もはや手遅れだ: the standard phrase of finality.

examples.ja: 彼はもはや以前のような若さはない。
examples.reading: かれはもはやいぜんのようなわかさはない。
examples.en: He no longer has the youthfulness he once had.
examples.note: With a negative: no longer has the youthfulness.

examples.ja: 紙の辞書はもはや珍しいものになった。
examples.reading: かみのじしょはもはやめずらしいものになった。
examples.en: Paper dictionaries have by now become a rarity.
examples.note: With an affirmative: paper dictionaries have by now become rare.

examples.ja: スマートフォンは、もはや生活に欠かせない存在だ。
examples.reading: スマートフォンは、もはやせいかつにかかせないそんざいだ。
examples.en: Smartphones have by now become indispensable to daily life.

examples.ja: 彼を説得することは、もはや不可能だと悟った。
examples.reading: かれをせっとくすることは、もはやふかのうだとさとった。
examples.en: I realised that persuading him was no longer possible.

similarGrammar.difference: "Ever since X, things have changed": marks the turning point rather than the present finality.
"Reaching the point of": also marks a stage reached, but as a verb phrase.
"Is in the process of changing": ongoing, whereas もはや says the change is complete.

commonMistakes.why: Everyday completed actions take もう; もはや is for irreversible changes of situation.
もはや and まだ contradict each other.
The predicate should show a situation that has changed for good, typically a negative or a final state.

usageNotes: もはやこれまでだ is a dramatic phrase meaning "this is the end".
It often appears in headlines and editorials about social change.
The feeling is one of finality; do not use it for everyday completions.
jlptTips: A formal sentence about an irreversible change + adverb blank → もはや.
Distractors: まだ, やがて, 今にも. Check the predicate: 手遅れ / 不可能 / 珍しくない point to もはや.
It can pair with both affirmative and negative predicates; do not assume it needs a negative.
